content.comment_body: Hello, I'm experiencing a major issue with my [product_name] web interface. I use the scheduler to switch lights on and off annually. The configuration options are: 1) range of years (for example, from 2000 to 2099), and 2) day/month for start and stop. The problem is, through the web server, I can only modify day and month, not the year range. When I adjust an available parameter, the end year automatically resets to 2000, which disables the scheduling feature since it's impossible to change the end year from the web interface. Since my clients rely solely on the web interface to manage their lighting, this makes the scheduler unusable if they change the day and month. Can someone assist me?

Using a weekly timer, you can set only the start/stop time and the weekdays; setting a year isn't possible. If you also need to configure the year, you must use a yearly timer together with a weekly timer.

Good morning [user_name], Based on the device (see attached image) and the documentation, the scheduler I'm using – not a weekly timer but a yearly one – should allow setting the specific start and stop dates (day and month). This works correctly in [product_name] simulation. The issue occurs when changing the time (month or day); the end year (highlighted in red in the image) automatically reverts to 2000. I have five of these clocks to manage holiday dates for my clients, during which the lighting must remain off. Thank you for the assistance.
Hi, I've attached a simplified example. Please check if you experience the same problem with it. Test it first, and then adjust as necessary. Let us know your findings. Good luck.
@[user_name], The question is about changing the year for on/off, not just the time.

Hello [user_name], My apologies if I misunderstood earlier. The switch-on and switch-off year parameters can only be changed via the web interface using the [product_name] variable change. Refer to the appendix. You need to assign these two parameters within [product_name] under Tools > VM assignment parameters.

My friend, please review: My understanding is that when the month or day is changed, the year also changes unintentionally. Your proposed solution is potentially a good approach to keep the year as needed.
Dear [user_name], Please find my test report attached. I may have made an error but can't identify where. Thank you for your assistance.

[user_name], Thanks for the detailed report! I don't see any issue with your method. This might be beyond what I can assist with. I recommend submitting a formal help request to [company_name]. Also, my friend [user_name] provided valuable input worth considering. Even if you don’t change the year, at least you can force it to the desired value. Good luck!

Thank you [user_name], Your solution allows users to set the year through the web interface, which is helpful. However, it's inconvenient that users must adjust day and month on one screen, and year on another list. It would be better if we could assign custom names to variables to manage all parameters from a single location.

Oh, now I understand what you mean. This appears to be an error with the web server. Watch the video in the attachment for clarification. You'll see how it’s possible to edit annual values via the web server as well. The accompanying sample shows how to program it accordingly.

Is it possible to make a controller program that keeps the year setting fixed? In other words, use memory variables but write static values to them. I tried but couldn't achieve this. This approach might help resolve the issue. Thanks.

analysis.insight_summary: Users relying on the [product_name] web interface to manage lighting schedules face a significant limitation: they can only adjust the day and month for annual events, but not the year range. Changing an available parameter online causes the end year to revert to 2000, which disables the scheduling feature. There is a partial workaround via the variable list, but this forces users to adjust settings in multiple places, negatively affecting the experience for customers who only have access through the web interface.
analysis.user_expectations: Users expect full, consistent remote access to all scheduling parameters—specifically, the ability to set both day/month and year range—directly from one area of the web interface, without needing to access and edit multiple parameter lists.
